preamble: Proto-Semitic emphatic *ṣ, reconstructed as the ejective affricate *tsʼ, is the plain affricate [ts] in Ashkenazi and Israeli Hebrew. Two accounts compete: loss of emphasis plus (re-)affrication under European contact (Hetzron 1987), or continuity of an old affricate, since the affricate reading of ṣādē goes back at least to medieval times and there is evidence for an affricate in Ancient Hebrew and Phoenician (Steiner 1982; Kogan 2011: 62–63). Either way the glottalization is lost; the route is debated. The Biblical Hebrew value of ṣ is not settled (Wiktionary gives /sˤ/, and /t͡sˤ/ ~ /sˤ/ for ארץ 'land'), so the entries start from Proto-Semitic. Yemenite Hebrew has [sˤ] (צדק /ˈsˤæ.ðæq/ 'justice'), and Wiktionary gives Sephardi צדק as /ˈse.dek/. Independently, stem-final *tsʼ lost its glottalization in Lower Tanana and Tanacross (Athabaskan).
